heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Hatchbox PETG natively out of the box with its stock stainless steel nozzle and direct drive extruder. Capable of reaching up to 167 mm/s based on an optimal volumetric flow rate of 14 mm³/s, printing with the front door cracked open prevents internal heat creep.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid release agent to prevent permanent bonding and PEI tear-out.
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed at 14 mm³/s in the Hatchbox PETG filament profile to avoid under-extrusion at high print speeds.
Set Pressure Advance to 0.038 s and enable a Wipe Distance of 1.0 mm to cleanly sever liquid PETG strings during travel moves.
Lower internal bridging fan speed to 60% and reduce auxiliary chamber fan to 0% to prevent rapid cooling, warpage, and brittle layer adhesion.
Set Z-Hop When Retracting to 0.4 mm with 'Spiral Lift' or 'Auto' selected to eliminate nozzle collision over delicate curled perimeters.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and Wispy Hairs Across Travel Gaps
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and possesses low melt viscosity, leading to ooze when moisture expands or retraction wipe is insufficient.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament at 65°C for 6 to 8 hours in an active dryer, set Retraction Distance to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s, and enable 'Wipe While Retracting' with 1.0 mm wipe distance.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Print Surface Chipping or Tearing PEI Coating
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG forms an extremely aggressive molecular bond to smooth and textured PEI sheets when printed without an interface boundary.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of PVA/PVP glue stick or dedicated liquid release agent to the bed before printing, and allow the bed to cool below 30°C before part removal.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder Clogging and Heat Creep Mid-Print
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Chamber ambient temperatures rise above 40°C in a fully closed P1S enclosure, causing PETG to soften before entering the melt zone.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Leave the front glass door ajar or tilt open the top glass cover during printing, while disabling the Auxiliary Part Fan.

faq.question: Should the Bambu Lab P1S enclosure door and top glass remain closed when printing Hatchbox PETG?
faq.answer: No, it is highly recommended to crack open the front glass door or vent the top glass lid to keep the chamber below 40°C and avoid heat creep in the direct drive extruder.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle to print Hatchbox PETG on the P1S?
faq.answer: No, standard Hatchbox PETG is non-abrasive, making the stock stainless steel 0.4 mm nozzle completely suitable for continuous production printing.

faq.question: Why is the Maximum Volumetric Speed restricted to 14 mm³/s instead of typical Bambu PLA speeds?
faq.answer: PETG has a higher melt viscosity than PLA, so limiting throughput to 14 mm³/s (approx 167 mm/s at 0.2mm layer height) guarantees complete thermal melting and strong interlayer bonds without under-extrusion.

faq.question: Can I use the Bambu Cool Plate or Smooth PEI Plate without glue for Hatchbox PETG?
faq.answer: Never print PETG directly on bare smooth PEI or the Cool Plate; PETG will permanently fuse to the sheet and tear the coating away upon removal. Always use glue stick as a release agent.
